body.p: A married man had a wife. She was like that: she would rant at her husband, she was a bad wife. Her husband got tired of her. THe husband left and walked through the taiga. At the foot of a mountain he found a lake, a round and deep one. He thinks: âI must call my wife and tell her: I found cranberries! I'll lie!â He went home and came home. The woman scolds him again: âWhere did you go for so long?â I was looking for berries, he says!â He, the man, began to work in his jurt.[StN]: Ð½Ð°ÑÐµÐ»? Ð¸ÑÐºÐ°Ð»? The woman says: âWhat did you find?â He says: 'I found cranberries on the mountain!' He was tired of her: âLet's go! Let's go! Let's go! I'll pick cranberries!â âWell, let's go!â â says the husband. So they go. As they walk, she keeps scolding her husband. They arrive at the lake. The husband says: âHere, on the lake, there are cranberries on the other [StN]: progrside!â She began to look over to the other side, to the lake. Then her husband pushed [her] into the lake. When she looked on the other side, he pushed her in. His wife fell into the lake â she drowned. She drowned and her husband went home. He stayed in the yurt, he stayed thereâ¦ He stayed in the yurt for a while, then he thought: ââI'll go and look at the lake! I'll go look at the lake! I'm going to lower the rope, the end of the rope â and see what happens there? He went, he took the rope, and came to the lake. He threw the rope, lowered the end [of the rope] into the lake. Then he pulled it up and caught someone on the rope. He pulled out the rope: a devil jumped out and caught him by the rope. âWhat?â [says the man?]. He [the devil] says: âI'm tired of the crooked woman! Let me go quickly!â â he says. The man pulled him, the little devil, out. The devil went and entered the rich man's brick hut. He knows that this devil would come. He goes to the top floor â it's dark. He hears: the devil is coming. He threw some bricks [StN]: INS - RUS â the devil has come.
